coreIdea: Identify recurrence SHAPE first (aT(n/b)+f(n) → Master Theorem; T(n-1)+f(n) → unroll/sum; T(n-1)+T(n-2) → exponential/Fibonacci-like).
mustRememberFormulas: Master Theorem: compare f(n) to n^(log_b a) — 3 cases
T(n)=2T(n/2)+n → Θ(n log n) (Merge Sort shape)

patternRecognitionTable.seeThis: recurrence given directly, asked to solve/classify it
recursive algorithm/code given, asked to SET UP the recurrence
asked exact/precise number of invocations (not just complexity class)
comparative TRUE/FALSE claim about a recurrence-defined function

commonTrapsQuickList: Don't force-fit Master Theorem onto shapes it doesn't cover (unequal splits, T(n-1)+T(n-2), log-factor boundary cases)
Count recursive calls carefully — missing a call site is the most common setup error
n^(log_b a) boundary case with an extra log factor needs recursion-tree, not basic Master Theorem
Call-count recurrence ≠ time-complexity recurrence when per-call work isn't constant
highYieldPyqLessons: Solving a given recurrence (20/36) is the dominant skill — know Master Theorem's 3 cases cold, and recursion-tree as the fallback.
Setting up a recurrence FROM code (12/36) is the reverse skill — practice both directions, they're tested almost equally.
